subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add native Gemini/project quota-bucket key-pool routing now, fold it into the broader provider-profile pool contract in #41135, or keep generic key/profile rotation plus external sidecar workarounds?
rationale: The source gap is real, but solving it requires choosing public config, persisted state, fallback timing, bucket semantics, and provider/plugin ownership that automation should not invent.

options.title: Fold Into #41135 With Gemini Slice
options.body: Use #41135 as the canonical design issue and define a minimal Gemini bucket-aware acceptance slice before implementation.

options.title: Land Narrow Embedded Key Rotation First
options.body: Keep bucket metadata out of scope and first prove same-run provider key-list rotation through embedded execution where key lists already exist.

options.title: Defer Native Core Policy
options.body: Keep generic key rotation and document external sidecar/proxy approaches until a plugin/API gap is clearer.

recommendation.title: Fold Into #41135 With Gemini Slice
recommendation.body: Use #41135 as the canonical design issue and define a minimal Gemini bucket-aware acceptance slice before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across generic key rotation, sticky auth-profile behavior, and model-failover docs.
